articles.title: As Fears of A.I. Catastrophe Magnify, Washington Stirs, but Mostly Slumbers
articles.author: David E. Sanger
articles.excerpt: President Trump has been in the forefront of the “what-me-worry?” crowd, refusing to engage on how to balance the risks and rewards of A.I.

articles.title: Lurking in Trump’s 9/11 Tribute, a Defense of His War With Iran
articles.author: David E. Sanger
articles.excerpt: The president appeared to embrace the idea that after 9/11, no risk can be tolerated, an echo of reasoning used by previous American officials in the “forever wars” that he has long denounced.

articles.title: When the Nation Was Attacked, Times Journalists Got to Work
articles.author: David E. Sanger
articles.excerpt: Seven reporters and editors at The New York Times reflect on the scenes they witnessed and the stories they wrote on Sept. 11, 2001.

articles.title: 25 Years After 9/11, Trump Personifies a Nation Moving On
articles.author: Peter Baker
articles.excerpt: The president has de-emphasized and shifted the war on terrorism at a time when fear of foreign attack has receded into the background of American life.

articles.title: 60 Posts in 10 Hours: How Trump’s Social Media Reflects His Version of Reality
articles.author: Peter Baker
articles.excerpt: With an assist from A.I., President Trump offers a window into how he wants to be seen — and, critics say, a barometer of his mental state.

articles.title: For Trump’s Former Fixer, a Tortured Path From ‘Rat’ to Reconciliation
articles.author: Peter Baker
articles.excerpt: The president has made peace with Michael D. Cohen, his onetime lawyer who turned against him. But contrary to Mr. Trump’s claims, Mr. Cohen has not recanted the testimony that helped convict his former boss.

articles.title: For Trump, the Iran War Is Stuck Between Combat and Genuine Peace
articles.author: Peter Baker
articles.excerpt: The war has deteriorated over the past six months into Mr. Trump’s own version of a “forever war,” with no clear goals and no end in sight.

articles.title: In Trump’s Washington, Ballooning National Debt Stirs Little Action
articles.author: Peter Baker
articles.excerpt: The relative indifference to the news that the U.S. government now owes $40 trillion demonstrates how drastically the politics of deficit spending has changed.

articles.title: At Home and Abroad, Deference to Trump Turns Increasingly to Defiance
articles.author: Peter Baker
articles.excerpt: While the president remains the most dominant figure in the world, other leaders and institutions are pushing back more vigorously than at the beginning of his second term.

articles.title: U.S. Attempt to Strangle Iran’s Economy Depends on China’s Cooperation
articles.author: David E. Sanger
articles.excerpt: The U.S. has spent 20 years promising ‘crippling sanctions’ on Iran. But the latest effort comes with a reverse twist, after military action failed to accomplish President Trump’s goals.

articles.title: Threatening Friends and Courting Enemies in Trump’s ‘Upside-Down World’
articles.author: Peter Baker
articles.excerpt: The president’s hostility to allies like Oman, Canada and South Korea, and his affection for adversaries like North Korea, may still shock some. But it comes as little surprise after a decade of upheaval.

articles.title: Facing Quagmire in Iran, Trump Turns to a Familiar Face: North Korea’s Kim Jong-un
articles.author: David E. Sanger
articles.excerpt: Seven years ago, President Trump failed to disarm North Korea and walked away. Could the same thing happen with Iran?

articles.title: In ‘The Brink of War,’ a Return to an Era of Razor-Edge Diplomacy
articles.author: Peter Baker
articles.excerpt: A new film depicts the 1986 nuclear arms summit in Reykjavik, Iceland, between Ronald Reagan and Mikhail Gorbachev, which both offered and dashed hopes of a dramatic breakthrough.

articles.title: As Iran War Turns Into Economic Battle, a New U.S. Strategy Recalls Old Ones
articles.author: David E. Sanger
articles.excerpt: The United States and Iran are poised to blow past a deadline they had set themselves to broker terms on peace and Iran’s nuclear program.

articles.title: How Do You Report on a Presidential Ruse?
articles.author: Peter Baker
articles.excerpt: President Trump’s Air Force One subterfuge duped potential adversaries — and the press. Here’s what happened.

articles.title: With Trump Secretly Evacuated, Imperiled Air Force One Became a Flying Decoy
articles.author: Peter Baker
articles.excerpt: In response to a threat against the jet last month, the president was clandestinely removed in a catering container. But the plane was sent into the skies anyway with government employees and reporters onboard.

articles.title: Insults, Expletives and Fat-Shaming: Vance Trolls Critics on the Right and Left
articles.author: Peter Baker
articles.excerpt: The vice president has dispensed with the decorum and restraint of his predecessors to directly take on opponents and journalists on social media with sometimes profane and often personal jabs.

articles.title: Trump’s Polling Numbers Hit a New Low. Don’t Expect Him to Change Course.
articles.author: Peter Baker
articles.excerpt: Barely a third of Americans approve of Mr. Trump’s handling of the job, putting him at historic depths for a second-term president at this stage of his tenure.

articles.title: At Graham’s Farewell, a Glimpse Into Power in Trump’s Washington
articles.author: Peter Baker
articles.excerpt: The political evolution of Lindsey Graham, the South Carolina senator, both captivated and confused many of his old friends but reflected the changing order in the nation’s capital.

articles.title: Trump Seems Trapped by Iran War, Even as He Wields the World’s Biggest Hammer
articles.author: David E. Sanger
articles.excerpt: A president who thought there were no limits to his power has discovered several, leaving him more frustrated and erratic.

articles.title: Why Is the U.S. Building the Saudi Nuclear Program While Destroying Iran’s?
articles.author: David E. Sanger
articles.excerpt: Our reporter explains what both countries are getting out of the deal.

articles.title: With His Latest Threats, Trump Signals to Iran That He Is Willing to Escalate
articles.author: David E. Sanger
articles.excerpt: President Trump is facing a critical moment in the war, which has failed to bring about the “unconditional surrender” he once demanded.

articles.title: How Presidential Travel Is the Ultimate Expression of Political Power
articles.author: Peter Baker
articles.excerpt: From horse-drawn presidential coaches to Air Force One, presidents have used various modes of transportation to project an image of America for nearly 250 years.

articles.title: Trump Promised Proof of Election Tampering. His Document Release Fell Far Short.
articles.author: David E. Sanger
articles.excerpt: In the end, the documentary evidence that President Trump claimed would prove his case appeared bound to disappoint those who expected bombshell revelations.

articles.title: A Trump Obsession That Carries a Cost for Democracy
articles.author: Peter Baker
articles.excerpt: In demanding steps to address the integrity of voting, President Trump persisted in relitigating his 2020 election defeat while finding ways to cast doubt on the 2026 outcome.

articles.title: In Iran, Trump Has Found an Opponent He Cannot Easily Dominate
articles.author: Peter Baker
articles.excerpt: The president is accustomed to forcing other countries to bend to his will. But he is struggling to come up with a strategy to extract Iranian concessions as the cease-fire he brokered collapses.

articles.title: Trump Says Fighting With Iran Has Resumed as He Orders Blockade and Tolls
articles.author: Peter Baker
articles.excerpt: After several days of strikes, the president notified Congress that fighting had begun again and announced shipping fees that his administration previously deemed illegal.

articles.title: How Lindsey Graham’s Journey From Trump Critic to Ally Made Him a Power Player
articles.author: Peter Baker
articles.excerpt: He initially called Donald Trump a “kook” who was “unfit for office,” only to join the new president’s Mar-a-Lago circle. “I’m still in the game,” Mr. Graham once explained of his much-analyzed turnabout.

articles.title: Bombing and a Tentative Accord Didn’t Work. Does Trump Have a Plan C for Iran?
articles.author: David E. Sanger
articles.excerpt: The administration appears to be reverting to an all-stick, no-carrot approach. But it has yet to answer why it believes economic warfare and bombing will yield a different result this time.

articles.title: As Iran Cease-Fire Frays, Trump Faces a Muddled War and Unpalatable Options
articles.author: David E. Sanger
articles.excerpt: The president appears to be confronting the consequences of a cease-fire deal cobbled together in haste, with little movement toward resolving the key issues driving the conflict.

articles.title: Trump Expected to Tell Turkey He Is Ready to Restore Access to F-35 Jets
articles.author: David E. Sanger
articles.excerpt: The president, who is headed to a NATO summit in Ankara this week, had imposed the ban himself amid concerns that giving Turkey the jets could allow Russia to learn about their stealth technology.

articles.title: Once the Centerpiece of Celebration, a Faded Declaration Recedes
articles.author: David E. Sanger
articles.excerpt: Sunlight and abuse have taken a toll on the document, encased in bulletproof glass. But the Trump administration “hasn’t put much emphasis on it,” a former archivist notes.

articles.title: NATO’s Leader Makes His Case to Trump for Preserving the Alliance
articles.author: David E. Sanger
articles.excerpt: Using charts, Secretary General Mark Rutte appeared to defuse the president’s anger by showing that European countries were “equalizing” defense spending with the U.S.

articles.title: Trump Is Making Big Claims About the Iran Talks. Iran Keeps Contradicting Him.
articles.author: David E. Sanger
articles.excerpt: President Trump appears to be describing his preferences as fully negotiated deals, in hopes of locking the Iranians in. The question is whether a succession of such disputes will sink the whole venture.
